headline: Scalable algorithms reduce memory and compute cost in genome-scale inference
label: Scalable Genomic Analysis Tools
summary: Datasets now reach thousands of human haplotypes and 100,000 taxa, making memory-efficient inference a practical requirement.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reducing the computational and memory cost of established genomic inference and comparison tasks while maintaining accuracy against reference results where reported. Moonshine.jl performs model-based ARG inference for thousands of human haplotypes in a single-threaded Julia implementation. STELAR-X scales triplet-based species tree inference under the multispecies coalescent to 100,000 taxa using O(nk) memory and GPU parallelism. clam estimates nucleotide diversity, divergence and FST from variant-only VCFs using callable loci, matching all-site results. LCSkPOA extends LCSk++ banding to POA graphs, reporting up to 98% memory savings and a 25x speedup on long reads. HAlign-G provides low-memory multiple genome alignment for closely related genomes. What is new is the transfer of banding and backbone seeding to graph representations, and the use of variant-only inputs.
